source.pc: In this skill you learn to add/subtract like fractions with variables, like turning into . This includes merging two fractions with equal denominator into one fraction, expanding any potential brackets in the numerator, and subsequently simplifying the numerator by merging similar terms. The skill does not include canceling fraction factors or merging fractions with different denominators.

If we add two number fractions with equal denominator, such as , then we know how to do so: add up the numerators to get . But how does this work when variables are involved, like when calculating ? The answer is: exactly the same. But there are a few things to pay attention to.

We want to add/subtract two fractions with variables, like Note that these two fractions have an equal denominator. As a result, they're called like fractions. (When the two fractions are not like fractions, they are harder to add up. This will be discussed in a follow-up skill. This current skill only deals with like fractions.)

To add/subtract two like fractions, the rule says to directly add/subtract the numerators, while keeping the denominator as it is.
